title: An entire American colony vanished and left one word behind
subject: Roanoke Colony

scenes.text: In fifteen ninety, a supply ship reached an English colony in North Carolina and found nobody there. Not one person.
One hundred and fifteen people. Men, women, children. All gone, and no sign of a fight.
The houses had been taken apart carefully. That is not what panic looks like.
Carved into a post was a single word. Croatoan. The name of an island fifty miles south.
The governor wanted to sail there. A storm hit, supplies ran low, and the ship turned back to England.
Nobody went looking again for three years. By then there was nothing left to find.
Four hundred years later we still do not know. What would you have done with that carving?

title: Nine hikers cut their way out of a tent from the inside
subject: Ural Mountains snow

scenes.text: Nine experienced hikers cut their tent open from the inside and ran into a snowstorm barefoot.
It was thirty below. Their boots, their coats, their food were all still inside.
Searchers found the tent a month later, sliced open along one wall. From within.
Some of the bodies were a mile downhill. A few had injuries that a fall could not explain.
The official report said a compelling natural force. That was the whole explanation.
In twenty nineteen, researchers modeled a small delayed slab avalanche. The numbers finally worked.
It explains the injuries. It still does not explain why they ran without their boots.

title: Bananas are radioactive and scientists actually use them as a unit
subject: banana fruit

scenes.text: Every banana you have ever eaten was radioactive. And that is completely fine.
Bananas are full of potassium, and a tiny slice of all potassium on Earth is potassium forty.
Potassium forty is unstable. It decays. Inside the banana, right now.
The dose is so small that physicists made a joke unit out of it. The banana equivalent dose.
One banana is about one percent of the radiation you get from a cross country flight.
Shipping containers of bananas have set off radiation detectors at ports. That really happens.
You would need about ten million bananas at once to be in danger. Good luck with that.

title: Archaeologists found honey that was still edible after three thousand years
subject: honey jar

scenes.text: Archaeologists opened an Egyptian tomb and found honey that was still perfectly edible.
Three thousand years old. Still good. No other food comes close.
Honey is almost entirely sugar and barely any water. Bacteria cannot live in it.
It also pulls water out of anything that lands in it, including the microbes.
And bees add an enzyme that makes a trace of hydrogen peroxide as it sits.
Acidic, dry and mildly antiseptic. That combination is why it simply does not spoil.
The honey in your kitchen right now could outlive your whole family line.

title: They were told to lick the brush. It was radium.
subject: Radium Girls

scenes.text: In nineteen seventeen, young women were hired to paint watch dials with glowing paint.
To keep a fine point, they were told to shape the brush with their lips. Over and over.
The paint was radium. Management knew. The chemists in the same building wore lead aprons.
The women painted their nails with it for fun. Some painted their teeth before dates.
Then their jaws began to break apart. The company blamed it on their personal lives.
Five of them sued while they were dying. The case took years and they won.
That verdict built the foundation of American workplace safety law. It cost them everything.

title: Australia declared war on birds and lost
subject: emu bird

scenes.text: In nineteen thirty two, the Australian army was sent to fight emus. Actual birds.
Twenty thousand of them were wrecking wheat farms in Western Australia.
So the government sent soldiers with two machine guns and ten thousand rounds.
The emus scattered into small groups and ran. They can hit thirty miles an hour.
One gun jammed. A truck chase ended when the truck hit a fence. The birds kept going.
After a week, the official count was about fifty birds. They pulled the troops out.
It is in the record books as the Emu War. Australia did not win it.

title: The coffee thing is a distraction and the math proves it
subject: coffee cup

scenes.text: You have been told to skip the coffee. That advice is aimed at the wrong number.
Say a daily coffee costs five dollars. That is about eighteen hundred a year.
Real, but small. Now look at rent, car and insurance. That is usually half of what you earn.
A one hundred dollar cut to a monthly bill saves twelve hundred a year, and you do it once.
The coffee decision costs you willpower every single morning. The bill does not.
This is illustrative math, not advice. Your numbers are different from mine.
So go look at your three biggest bills first. The coffee can wait.

title: The self-checkout machine has decided you are a criminal
subject: grocery store aisle

scenes.text: The self-checkout machine does not think you are a customer. It thinks you are a suspect.
You scan one apple. Unexpected item in the bagging area. Sir, that is the apple.
You move the apple. Please place the item in the bagging area. Pick a side.
Now the light on top is spinning and everyone in line knows you did something.
An employee walks over, taps the screen twice, and walks away. Never says a word.
Two taps. That is all it was. You stood there for four minutes like a hostage.
And the machine still thanked you for shopping. It knows exactly what it did.

title: Nobody has ever successfully left a group chat
subject: smartphone screen

scenes.text: Getting added to a group chat takes one second. Getting out takes an act of Congress.
Someone starts it to plan one dinner. Two years later it is still going.
The dinner happened. The chat never acknowledged this and moved on to memes.
There is one person who only replies with a thumbs up. To everything. Including bad news.
And one who types for ninety seconds and then sends the word ok.
You mute it. You do not leave it. Leaving is a statement and you are not ready.
Four hundred unread and you will read every one. Tonight. At two in the morning.
